title: Body cavities and abdominal regions: quadrants and nine-region map
description: Understand dorsal, ventral, thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities, serous spaces, four quadrants and nine patient-oriented abdominal regions.

questions.question: What are the dorsal and ventral body cavities?
questions.answer: The dorsal compartment includes cranial and vertebral cavities containing the central nervous system. The ventral compartment is commonly divided by the diaphragm into thoracic and abdominopelvic regions.

questions.question: Which body cavity contains the heart?
questions.answer: The heart is in the thorax, in the middle mediastinum. It is enclosed by a pericardial sac; the pericardial cavity is the thin potential space between the serous pericardial layers.

questions.question: Where are the kidneys in relation to the peritoneum?
questions.answer: The kidneys lie retroperitoneally, posterior to the parietal peritoneum. They are not floating inside the potential peritoneal cavity.

questions.question: What are the four abdominal quadrants?
questions.answer: A vertical and a horizontal line crossing at the umbilicus form the patient's right upper, left upper, right lower and left lower quadrants. These are surface-location guides, not exact organ outlines.

questions.question: How do the nine abdominal regions differ from quadrants?
questions.answer: The nine-region system uses a three-by-three arrangement: hypochondriac, epigastric; lumbar, umbilical; and iliac, hypogastric positions. Right and left always refer to the patient, not the person viewing the image.
